payload.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/checklist.json:376 and proofstory.json:49 now promise that the Windows branch validates the npm command-shim contract, but packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:693-695 returns true for every win32 bin target solely from the platform value, while inspectGlobalCoreExecutable at :737-769 only stats the declared dist/cli.js file and never locates, reads, or validates a generated proof-or-stop.cmd/.ps1 shim. The alleged Windows regression at packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:1229-1240 likewise creates no command shim; it merely injects platform=win32 and asserts that the unconditional true is returned. A missing, stale, or malformed global Windows shim can therefore coexist with executable=yes and the global-core-realpath PASS marker. F-026's resolution claim is not delivered: either validate the actual shim/target relationship or narrow the Story contract and finding resolution to the Node-target-only fact. severity: critical

quality-win32-command-path-percent-expansion: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:703-707 states that wrapping a Windows path in double quotes is sufficient for cmd.exe metacharacters, and the F-028 resolution relies on this helper for cd /d, npm --prefix, and dir remediation. That is false for the legal Windows filename character `%`: cmd.exe expands `%NAME%` even inside double quotes, so a canonical checkout such as C:\\work\\%TEMP%\\Prooforstop is rewritten to the environment variable value and every emitted remediation targets the wrong path. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:172-184 mirrors the same incomplete quoting and its Windows case uses only a space-containing POSIX temp path, so it cannot catch percent expansion. F-028 is therefore not fully resolved for valid Windows paths; render an actually literal cmd.exe path representation or constrain/report unsupported paths, with a regression containing paired percent signs. severity: medium

test-coverage-win32-capability-skip-false-pass: packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:83-87 handles an unavailable Windows directory-link capability by printing `ok global-core-realpath` and exiting 0 before any of cases 1-34 run. All three CHK-003 must intents pin exactly that selector, so on an EPERM/EACCES/ENOSYS Windows host the CLI can issue passing mechanical receipts for canonical/drift/non-git, platform executable semantics, and adversarial remediation while executing zero assertions—including the supposedly every-host win32 case 34 at :1224-1284. This is a distinct evidence-integrity gap beyond F-029 (no real shim validation) and F-030 (cmd percent quoting): the F-026 portability repair changed a setup failure into an indistinguishable green result. Limit the skip to link-dependent cases or introduce a fixture seam for the platform-only assertions, and ensure skipped execution cannot match the acceptance selector. severity: high
